knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(terra)
library(foreign)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(rnaturalearth) #for basemaps
library(ggsci) #for color palettes
library(leaflet) #for interactive maps
```

```{r}
#these are in VicGrid on GDA94 projections
bioregions <- read_sf("Bioregions_shapefile/Bioregions.shp")
```


```{r}
fish <- read_csv("fishMaster.csv")
invert <- read_csv("invertMaster.csv")
```

```{r}
# convert survey points to sf object
surveys_sf <- st_as_sf(fish, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326)

# make sure bioregions are in the same CRS
bioregions <- st_transform(bioregions, crs = st_crs(surveys_sf))

# spatial join - matches each point to the polygon it falls within
surveys_with_bioregion <- st_join(surveys_sf, bioregions, join = st_within)

# select just the columns you need
result_fish <- surveys_with_bioregion |>
  dplyr::select(survey_id, survey_date, MESO_NAME)
```


```{r}
# convert survey points to sf object
surveys_sf <- st_as_sf(invert, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326)

# make sure bioregions are in the same CRS
bioregions <- st_transform(bioregions, crs = st_crs(surveys_sf))

# spatial join - matches each point to the polygon it falls within
surveys_with_bioregion <- st_join(surveys_sf, bioregions, join = st_within)

# select just the columns you need
result_invert <- surveys_with_bioregion |>
  dplyr::select(survey_id, survey_date, MESO_NAME)
```

```{r}
result_fish <- result_fish |>
  mutate(
    longitude = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 1],
    latitude = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 2]
  ) |>
  st_drop_geometry()

result_fish <- result_fish |>
  rename(bioregion = MESO_NAME)

result_invert <- result_invert |>
  mutate(
    longitude = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 1],
    latitude = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 2]
  ) |>
  st_drop_geometry()

result_invert <- result_invert |>
  rename(bioregion = MESO_NAME)
```

```{r}
pts <- st_as_sf(result_fish, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326)

# 2. Split into known and unknown bioregions
known <- pts %>% filter(!is.na(bioregion))
unknown <- pts %>% filter(is.na(bioregion))

# 3. Find nearest known neighbor for each unknown point
nn_index <- st_nearest_feature(unknown, known)

# 4. Pull bioregions from nearest known points
unknown$bioregion <- known$bioregion[nn_index]

# 5. Combine back together
filled_fish <- bind_rows(known, unknown) %>% 
  arrange(row_number())
```

```{r}
pts <- st_as_sf(result_invert, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326)

# 2. Split into known and unknown bioregions
known <- pts %>% filter(!is.na(bioregion))
unknown <- pts %>% filter(is.na(bioregion))

# 3. Find nearest known neighbor for each unknown point
nn_index <- st_nearest_feature(unknown, known)

# 4. Pull bioregions from nearest known points
unknown$bioregion <- known$bioregion[nn_index]

# 5. Combine back together
filled_invert <- bind_rows(known, unknown) %>% 
  arrange(row_number())
```


```{r}
regions_fish <- st_drop_geometry(filled_fish)

regions_invert <- st_drop_geometry(filled_invert)
```

```{r}
write_csv(regions_fish, "bioregionsFish.csv")
write_csv(regions_invert, "bioregionsInvert.csv")
```

# This is Troubleshooting Code that probably won't work in the future bc combined is from combinedCorrectResolutions

okay so let's hope that you don't have to do this again, because what you did was combine the results from the section above (bioregionsFish and bioregionsInvert) with the rest of the dataset in the combinedCorrectResolutions code, and then brought that back to the code below to match nearest neighbors and correct it, which is then saved and put back into combinedCorrectResolutions :)

```{r}
fish <- read_csv("combinedFish.csv")
fish <- fish |>
  dplyr::select(latitude, longitude, bioregion, location)

invert <- read_csv("combinedInvert.csv")
invert <- invert |>
  dplyr::select(latitude, longitude, bioregion, location)
```



(leaflet maps to ID NA areas)

```{r}
# extract d3 colours
d3_colours <- pal_d3()(length(unique(invert$bioregion)))

# use in leaflet
pal <- colorFactor(palette = d3_colours, domain = invert$bioregion)

leaflet(fish, width = "100%") |>
  addTiles() |>  # adds OpenStreetMap basemap
  addCircleMarkers(
    lng = ~longitude,
    lat = ~latitude,
    color = ~pal(bioregion),
    label = ~paste(location, bioregion, latitude, longitude, sep = " | "), #shows on hover
    radius = 5,
    fillOpacity = 1
  ) |>
  addLegend(
    position = "bottomright",
    pal = pal,
    values = ~bioregion,
    title = "Location"
  )
```
